title: after compset -P, zshrs leaves the matched prefix on the command line; zsh removes it

observed.notes: `compset -P '*\='` moves 'a=b=' into IPREFIX, then an ambiguous `compadd -U -Q -- xx yy` is made. zsh redraws the line without the IPREFIX text; zshrs keeps it. The cursor column follows the text.

variants.note: fuzz-found witness this probe was distilled from, confirmed 2026-08-30 (FAIL, 1 row): zsh '@SFZ@ fzc0001' vs zshrs '@SFZ@ fzc0001 a='.

spec.completer:
#compdef fzc0001

local -a _sfz_hit
compset -P '*\=' && _sfz_hit+=( 'hit:P:*\=' )

compadd -U -Q -J _sfzprobe -X 'compset state' -- "PRE=$PREFIX" "SUF=$SUFFIX" "IPRE=$IPREFIX" "ISUF=$ISUFFIX" "QIPRE=$QIPREFIX" "QISUF=$QISUFFIX" "CUR=$CURRENT" "WORDS=${(j:|:)words}" "HIT=${(j:,:)_sfz_hit}"

compadd -- alpha beta gamma

confirmed.note: all three harness files had uncommitted edits when this was confirmed (three agents were editing them concurrently); the sha256 prefixes above pin the exact bytes used.
